subtopics.title: What Internal Control Is — and What It Protects

questions.question: Internal control is best defined as:
options: The security guards a business employs
The system of policies, procedures and checks that safeguards assets, ensures accurate records, promotes efficiency and encourages adherence to policies
The owner personally watching every worker

questions.question: Division of duties means:
options: Every worker gets an equal share of tasks
Managers do the important work themselves
No single person controls a transaction from beginning to end

questions.question: Internal control assumes that:
options: Errors never happen in a well-run business
People are human — so the structure must surface errors quickly and make dishonesty difficult and detectable

subtopics.title: The Five Components of Internal Control

questions.question: An owner who takes cash from the till for private use damages which component most directly?
options: The control environment — the tone at the top that makes every other control credible

questions.question: Deliberately asking 'where can stock disappear and which records could be manipulated?' is:
Surprise cash counts and comparing the annual stocktake against the records belong to:
options: Monitoring — checking that controls work in practice, not only on paper

questions.question: A sensible rule that no staff member was ever told about fails because of weak:
Numbered source documents are a control because:
options: A missing number in the sequence immediately raises a question that demands an answer

questions.question: Which arrangement shows correct division of duties for cash?
options: The person who receives cash also records and banks it
The cashier receives cash, a different person records it, and banking is checked against the records
Whoever is free at closing counts the till alone

questions.question: Comparing the bank statement against the cash journals is an example of:
options: An independent check (reconciliation) — two independently created records that must agree

subtopics.title: Reading a Scenario Like an Examiner

questions.question: The three-move answer to any internal-control scenario is:
options: Quote the definition, name the owner, suggest a meeting
Identify the weakness, explain the concrete risk, recommend a specific control
List all five components, then choose one
Calculate the loss, blame the employee, add security cameras

questions.question: Why does 'the owner must be more careful' earn no marks as a recommendation?
options: Recommendations must criticise employees, not owners
It is not specific or actionable — a control must name who does what differently
It is too short for the mark allocation

questions.question: Takings kept in a drawer and banked 'whenever there is time' should be answered with:
options: Weakness: cash not banked promptly; risk: theft, loss and unverifiable records; control: bank daily and intact, reconciling deposits against the cash journal
Weakness: too much cash; risk: none if staff are trusted; control: a bigger drawer
Weakness: no computer; risk: slow service; control: buy software
Weakness: banking fees; risk: high costs; control: bank monthly

questions.question: In the one-person tuck shop, why can nobody — including Sipho — prove whether money was taken?
options: The float was too small to count
No separate cash box, no records, no counting: honesty and theft produce identical evidence — none

questions.question: The three-learner version (money, stock and recording split; box counted by two) mainly demonstrates:
options: Division of duties with independent checking

questions.question: The lesson says a good control system PROTECTS honest workers because:
options: It hides small mistakes from managers
When the box matches the notebook, their honesty is provable instead of merely hoped
It prevents them being given difficult duties
It guarantees nobody is ever suspected

subtopics.title: Five Questions Every Business Must Answer

questions.question: 'Who sets the example?' is the plain version of which component?
A teacher who borrows from the cash box 'till Monday' teaches learners that:
options: The box is borrowable — the example at the top has made the rules unreal
The box needs a better lock

questions.question: The treasurer doing a surprise count at break answers which plain question?
options: Who checks that the rules still happen?
Does everyone know what is happening?

subtopics.title: Spot the Weakness — Your Turn on Patrol

questions.question: The nephew running the spaza alone and paying his own wages from the tin is primarily a failure of:
options: Division of duties and documentation — one person, all roles, self-served wages from unrecorded cash

questions.question: The storeroom standing open on delivery days is best fixed by:
options: Buying more stock so losses matter less
Keeping it locked, with one named person receiving deliveries and counting them against the delivery note

questions.question: Unnumbered receipts written 'when the customer asks' are dangerous because:
options: A missing receipt is invisible, so recorded income becomes whatever happened to be written down
